headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and cascading-error exposure between Flowise and Prefect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while Prefect can consume workflow metadata and broad egress. A shared workspace or file handoff makes prompt injection plausible, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this stays below high.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled content into a shared file that Prefect later parses as instructions
IF both are deployed against the same server datastore or workspace
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all shared artifacts
Require human review before Prefect consumes Flowise outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and Prefect handles workflow metadata with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive chatflow content can flow into Prefect outputs or remote calls. The profiles do not prove a shared OS workspace, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF Flowise stores chatflow outputs in a location Prefect can read
IF Prefect forwards workflow metadata to external services
mitigations: Use separate storage buckets or directories
Audit shared artifacts for sensitive fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has filesystem write access and broad egress; Prefect also has broad egress and can call GitHub APIs. Overlap on mutable shared resources is plausible, but the profiles do not show both writing the same directory or git state, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory
IF an orchestrator lets both mutate the same workflow metadata without locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and Prefect is an orchestration/pipeline system that can act on workflow metadata. If Prefect treats Flowise output as authoritative, bad facts can cascade into downstream actions; because this is a default orchestration pattern and can trigger irreversible operational mistakes, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Flowise-generated artifacts without verification
IF those artifacts drive downstream pipeline actions or notifications
mitigations: Require schema checks on all Flowise outputs
Add human approval for action-taking tasks
Log and diff all downstream decisions

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch chatflow inputs/outputs or workflow metadata, so no specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. The main compliance concern is generic logging/retention drift if shared artifacts contain sensitive content, but the profiles do not establish a concrete regulated-data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared workflow metadata
IF retention policies differ for the shared artifacts
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared metadata
Document data-class handling for both agents
